insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited

great.name: Co-pay
great.quote: Co-payment means a cost sharing requirement under a health insurance policy that provides that the policyholder/ insured/ proposer will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claims amount.
great.explanation: Only a glossary definition of co-payment is given and no applied co-pay clause is stated here. No co-pay is charged on this plan — the insurer bears 100% of all admissible claims, which is better than many policies that add 10–20% co-pay for seniors.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Pre-existing diseases: Covered after 24 months (48 months, for plans with Sum Insured up to 2Lacs) of continuous coverage.
good.reference: Key Information Sheet, S.No 6(a); Policy Wording Part II, Clause 3.1
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 24 months of continuous coverage, but it becomes 48 months if Sum Insured is up to ₹2 lakhs. This means you must keep the policy active for 2–4 years before claiming for declared pre-existing conditions.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.explanation: Listed specific illnesses/surgeries are not covered until 24 months of continuous coverage are completed. Claims for these conditions will be payable only from the 3rd policy year onwards.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Initial waiting period: 30 days for all illnesses (except Hospitalisation due to injury).
good.reference: Key Information Sheet, S.No 6(d); Policy Wording Part II, Clause 3.4
good.explanation: Illness-related hospitalisation is covered only after a 30-day waiting period, while hospitalisation due to injury is covered immediately. This blocks claims for illnesses that start in the first month.

good.name: Restore Benefit
good.quote: For plans with Sum Insured ` 3lacs and above, We will reset up to 100% of the Sum insured once in a policy year... The reset amount can only be used for all future claims within the same policy year, not related to the illness/ disease/ injury for which a claim has been paid in that policy year for the same person
good.reference: Policy Wording Part II, Section 2 (Scope of Cover), E) Reset Benefit
good.explanation: For Sum Insured ₹3 lakhs and above, up to 100% of the Sum Insured is restored once in a policy year. The restored amount can be used only for unrelated future claims for the same person in that year.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Pre-hospitalisation Medical Expenses incurred by You for a 30-day period immediately prior to Your Hospitalisation
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 30 days before hospitalisation are covered. This helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading up to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Post-hospitalisation Medical Expenses incurred by You for a 60-day period immediately post Hospitalisation
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days after discharge are covered. This reduces out-of-pocket costs for follow-ups and medicines during recovery.

good.name: NCB
good.quote: An Additional Sum Insured of 10% of Annual Sum Insured provided on each renewal for every claim-free year up to a maximum of 50%. In case of a claim under the policy, the accumulated Additional Sum Insured will be reduced by 10% of the Annual Sum Insured in the following year.
good.reference: Key Information Sheet, S.No 10(a); Policy Wording Part II, Section 2(G) Additional Sum Insured (Cumulative Bonus)
good.explanation: An additional sum insured of 10% is added each claim-free renewal up to 50%, and after a claim it reduces by 10% of the Annual Sum Insured next year. This means the bonus does not reset to zero in one claim, so your increased cover is partly retained.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Below are the non payable items applicable in the policy... GLOVES... SYRINGES / PPE-type items etc. (listed as non payable items)
bad.reference: Policy document section: "Non Payables" / "List of Non Payable Items as per IRDAI"
bad.explanation: Common hospital consumables (like gloves, syringes and PPE-type items) are listed as non-payable. This can add meaningful out-of-pocket costs during hospitalisation even when the main bill is covered.

bad.name: Cashless Network
bad.quote: Cashless Facility available at over 4000+ network hospitals.
bad.explanation: Cashless treatment is available at 4000+ network hospitals. A smaller network can limit cashless options in your city and may force reimbursement claims.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: Cataract, where sub-limit of ` 20,000/- is applicable per eye per Policy year for Plans with Sum Insured up to 5 Lacs. Sub limit of ` 1,00,000 per eye per Policy year will be applicable for cataract treatment for plans with Sum Insured above ` 5Lacs
bad.reference: Key Information Sheet, S.No 8(a); Policy Wording Part II, Clause 3.2 (Cataract*)
bad.explanation: Cataract has a sub-limit of ₹20,000 per eye per policy year for Sum Insured up to ₹5 lakhs, and ₹1,00,000 per eye per policy year above ₹5 lakhs. If your hospital charges more than this cap, you will pay the difference.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: Extension 15: Sub Limits on Medical Expenses/ Illness/ Surgeries/ Procedures... Our maximum liability... shall be limited as per the table below
bad.explanation: If Extension 15 is opted, the insurer’s payout is capped for listed illnesses/surgeries/procedures as per a table. These sub-limits can sharply reduce claim payouts for common treatments.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
